On page 31, the Statement points out that "natural areas of the National Park System and of the National Wildlife Refuge System would have their basic program missions compromised if ORV use were permitted on them." This conclusion is supported by Interior's own Off-road Recreation Vehicle Task Force Study, which states on page 30, "ORV use ... is basically incompatible with the primary purpose of the Refuge System." Therefore the Secretary's memorandum, which allows ORV use on the Wildlife Refuges if the responsible bureau head determines that the use will not damage resources, should be changed to forbid ORV use in these areas.
On other lands administered by the Department, the Classification and Multiple Use Act of 1964, 43 USC 1411-18, requires that the Secretary classify retained Federal lands by use category. Among the uses permitted for retained lands are " ... (6) outdoor recreation ... or (10) preservation of public values that would be lost if the land passed from Federal ownership." 43 USC 1411(a) In making determinations, the Secretary is required to " ... give due consideration to all pertinent factors, including but not limited to, ecology, priorities of use, and the relative values of the various resources in particular areas." 43 USC 1411(b)
Use priorities are necessary whenever lands are suitable for incompatible uses; e.g., ORV use and wildlife study. These priorities must take account of the environmental impacts of the competing uses, and give preference to uses which do not impair basic environmental values.
